voice.name: ash
voice.instructions: A calm, clear explainer narrator for researchers. Warm and unhurried, plain-spoken, with natural pauses between ideas. Friendly, never salesy.

shots.name: welcome
vo: Research runs on papers: finding them, reading them, understanding them, and building on them.
Koios is one place for all of it. Here is how it works.

shots.name: find-query
shots.caption: One search box, *every* index.
shots.vo: It starts with one search box. Type a topic, and choose where to look: arXiv, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Google Scholar, even books and PDFs.

shots.name: find-results
shots.caption: Asked at once, merged into *one* list.
shots.vo: Koios asks them all at once, and merges the answers: a paper several indexes know shows up once, with the best of what each knows.

shots.name: find-copies
shots.caption: Every place a paper can be read.
shots.vo: Open a result to see every place it can be read: the preprint, the published version, repository copies. One click saves it to a collection, with Undo.

shots.name: find-people
shots.caption: Search for *people*, too.
vo: Search for a person, and you get their profile:
where they work, their citations and h-index, and everything they have written, newest first or most cited.

shots.name: find-poster
shots.caption: It reads the *paper*, not the poster.
vo: When you open a paper, Koios tries each copy until one hands over the real thing.
Here the first copy was the conference poster. It was passed over, and the list says why.

shots.name: home-views
shots.caption: Everything you keep, on *Home*.
shots.vo: Everything you save lives on Home: your collections, what you are reading, and what to read next.

shots.name: home-continue
shots.caption: Pick up *exactly* where you stopped.
shots.vo: Continue reading shows the very page where you stopped: what you have read is dimmed, with a line where you left off.

shots.name: home-plan
shots.caption: A plan for *today*, and what's new.
shots.vo: Today turns your library into a short plan. Inbox gathers the papers that arrived since your last visit.

shots.name: home-collections
shots.caption: Collections: drag a paper where it belongs.
shots.vo: Collections lay your papers out in columns. Drag one across to move it.

shots.name: home-desk
shots.caption: *R*: your desk. Every paper in progress.
vo: Resume, and you are back on the page.
Press R for your desk: every paper in progress, side by side, each at the line you left it. G takes you home.

shots.name: read-modes
shots.caption: As typeset, or *reflowed* to read.
shots.vo: Read a paper as it was typeset, or switch to Reflow: the same text, laid out to read comfortably at any width.

shots.name: read-book
shots.caption: Or as a *book*.
shots.vo: Or as a book, two pages side by side, turned with the arrow keys.

shots.name: read-look
shots.caption: Zoom, a *loupe*, and figures up close.
vo: Zoom in, with a map to find your way.
L brings out a loupe. C lifts a figure off the page, full screen, caption and all.

shots.name: read-zen
shots.caption: *Z*: just you and the page.
shots.vo: And Z is zen: everything else falls away.

shots.name: highlight
shots.caption: Highlight, in PDF *and* Reflow.
shots.vo: Select a passage to highlight it. The same marks show in the PDF and in Reflow.

shots.name: lookup
shots.caption: Right-click: what it *means*, where it *comes from*.
vo: Right-click a term, and a card opens beside it, never over it.
What the word means. Where the idea comes from, with the earliest papers to use it. And a comment, which highlights the passage as you type.

shots.name: hover
shots.caption: Hover an author, or a *citation*.
shots.vo: Rest the pointer on an author to see who they are, or on a citation for the paper it points to.

shots.name: notes
shots.caption: Your notes, by section, and a *board*.
vo: Keep a figure in your notes with one click.
H opens your notes: every highlight and comment, by section. B spreads them on a board, to think with.

shots.name: sticky
shots.caption: *M* pins a sticky to the page.
shots.vo: And M pins a sticky note right onto the page.

shots.name: ask-open
shots.caption: Ask about *what's on your screen*.
vo: Press Control and backslash, and Ask AI floats over the page.
It reads what is on your screen with every question, so there is nothing to paste.

shots.name: ask-passages
shots.caption: Every answer *points* at the paper.
shots.vo: An answer that rests on the paper lists the passages it used. The paper scrolls to the first and marks it; click another, and it goes there.

shots.name: ask-figure
shots.caption: Ask about a *figure*.
shots.vo: Send a screenshot with your question, and ask about a figure. Answers can draw the paper's own figures inline.

shots.name: ask-models
shots.caption: Claude, DeepSeek or Gemini: *your* pick.
shots.vo: Pick the model: Claude, DeepSeek or Gemini. Switch between questions; the conversation goes along.

shots.name: ask-web
shots.caption: Search the *web*, with sources.
shots.vo: Turn on the globe, and it can search the web and read pages, listing each one, and linking its sources in the answer.

shots.name: ask-papers
shots.caption: Papers it names, *one click* from your library.
shots.vo: Papers it mentions become cards you can find or save, all at once if you like.

shots.name: ask-window
shots.caption: History, looks, and *docking*.
shots.vo: Every chat is kept in your history. And the window is yours to arrange: drag it, restyle it, or dock it beside the page.

shots.name: explain
shots.caption: Press *E*: the whole paper, explained.
vo: Press E, and the whole paper is explained, section by section.
The claim, the mechanism, the maths worked through, and how it has held up since.

shots.name: implement
shots.caption: Plan the *implementation*.
shots.vo: The Implementation tab plans how to build it yourself: what to reproduce, which datasets, a repository layout, and what it will cost on your hardware.

shots.name: colab
shots.caption: A notebook from the paper, *run* on Colab.
vo: Then a notebook is written from the paper, and run on Google Colab:
here on a T4 GPU, with the machine's load read live, beside the cells.

shots.name: project
shots.caption: From a paper to a *project*.
vo: Start a project from a paper.
It opens like an editor you know: the paper's files in it, the abstract in the README, and the implementation written in one go if you want.

shots.name: agents
shots.caption: Claude Code, Codex, or Koios AI: *your* agent.
shots.vo: Beside it, an agent that has read the paper. Choose Claude Code, Codex, the built-in Koios AI, or a plain terminal.

shots.name: agent-work
shots.caption: It reads, writes, and *runs* the tests.
vo: Ask for a piece of the paper, with a test.
It reads the paper, writes the files, runs the tests on your machine, and reads the result. Every change can be undone at once.

shots.name: vscode
shots.caption: Or open it in *VS Code*.
vo: Prefer VS Code? Open the project in it, or right here in the page.
The Koios extension lists your projects and the papers they cite, and a citation in the code is a link back to the paper.

shots.name: sim-pick
shots.caption: *31* simulators, one click away.
vo: For reinforcement learning, start from a simulation.
Thirty-one simulators: classic control, MuJoCo locomotion, robot arms and hands, games, driving, 3D worlds. Each says what it needs, and whether it runs on Colab.

shots.name: sim-start
shots.caption: PPO, SAC, a world model: *start* from one.
shots.vo: Pick an environment and a starting point: PPO or SAC in one readable file, Stable-Baselines, or a world model. Choose where it runs, and the project is made.

shots.name: sim-watch
shots.caption: Watch it *learn*, live.
vo: The Sim pane reads the run as it goes:
the agent live, the return climbing, recorded videos, and every number, with findings on what is going right or wrong.

shots.name: sim-dream
shots.caption: A world model's *dreams*, against the real thing.
shots.vo: A world model's dreams play beside reality, with how far they drift.

shots.name: sim-filed
shots.caption: Every run, *filed* in your logbook.
shots.vo: And every finished run is filed by itself, in the project's logbook, with its results and notes written for you.

shots.name: companion-get
shots.caption: The *Companion* connects your computer.
vo: Your code can run on your own computers too, through the Companion.
It is a small program: inside the desktop app for Mac, Windows or Linux, one terminal command, or with the VS Code extension.

shots.name: companion-pair
shots.caption: Paired *once*. No tokens to paste.
shots.vo: Once it runs, Koios finds it. Type the code it shows, and connect. That is the whole setup.

shots.name: anywhere-you
shots.vo: Here is what that makes possible. You can work from anywhere: any browser, a café, the library, the lab.

shots.name: anywhere-code
shots.vo: Your code lives on a computer of yours. The Companion keeps the project folder, its Python, and a terminal.

shots.name: anywhere-compute
shots.vo: The compute can be somewhere bigger: a Colab GPU, or your lab's server. It reads your folder live, over a secure tunnel; nothing is copied first.

shots.name: anywhere-data
shots.vo: The data has a place of its own, Google Drive by default: datasets come in, checkpoints and logs go out, never back over the wire.

shots.name: anywhere-watch
vo: And you watch the output live, wherever you are,
and can pick the run up later, from another computer.

shots.name: anywhere-all
shots.vo: Code here. Compute there. Data in Drive. You, anywhere.

shots.name: split
shots.caption: Code on your laptop, *compute* on a GPU.
vo: Here it is for real.
A new project: its code kept on the laptop, its compute on the lab's A100.

shots.name: koios-run
shots.caption: *koios run*: your files, the GPU's power.
vo: In the terminal, by your files, koios run sends the script to the GPU, and its output comes straight back.
A second tab is a shell on the GPU itself.

shots.name: mount
shots.caption: Your folder, *mounted* live on the GPU.
shots.vo: Switch on the mount, and the GPU reads your folder live, as if it were its own disk.

shots.name: data-place
shots.caption: Choose where *data and results* go.
shots.vo: Storage and compute say where everything is: the files on your laptop, and where data and results are kept.

shots.name: machines
shots.caption: Many machines, *one* project.
vo: Add more machines to the same project: Colab GPUs, a lab server, your laptop.
Settings shows them all, which are running, and keeps the Companion up to date.

shots.name: together
shots.caption: See who's here, and *follow* along.
vo: Research is rarely solo.
Projects gather the papers, the people and the work. See who is here, what they are looking at, and follow along, live.

shots.name: bibliography
shots.caption: A bibliography you can *trust*.
shots.vo: Each project keeps its papers by role, and a bibliography where the published version's BibTeX is one click away.

shots.name: write
shots.caption: Write, and *cite* as you go.
vo: Write the paper beside your reading: LaTeX that compiles as you go, in sync with Overleaf.
Put the cursor after a claim, and Koios suggests what to cite. One click adds it, and the reference appears in the PDF.

shots.name: logbook
shots.caption: A logbook, a whiteboard, your calendar.
shots.vo: A logbook keeps the meetings, the links and a shared whiteboard, and your calendar is right beside them.

shots.name: end

card.sub: koios.dev  ·  in your browser, or download the app

shots.vo: Koios. Find it, read it, understand it, then run it. At koios dot dev.
